scope: Theorem 1.1 of the manuscript “The Isoperimetric Conjecture for the Cubic Flat Three-Torus” (preprints/The-Isoperimetric-Conjecture-for-the-Cubic-Flat-Three-Torus-September-24-2026/article.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 354 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 ce66c455780d2efc), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 1. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For V ∈ (0, 1), put v = min(V, 1 − V ). Among finite-perimeter subsets of R3/Z3 of volume V , the minimum perimeter is Iunit(V ) = min n (36π)1/3 v2/3 , 2 √ πv, 2 o . (1.1) For 0 < V ≤ 1/2, every minimizing region is, up to an ambient isometry and a null set, one of the following: volume range region 0 < V ≤ 4π/81 a ball of radius (3V/(4π))1/3 4π/81 ≤ V ≤ 1/π a solid circular tube of radius p V/π about a shortest closed geodesic 1/π ≤ V ≤ 1/2 a slab of width V between coordinate tori. Both listed types occur at each common endpoint of adjacent ranges, and there are no further equality cases. For V > 1/2, the minimizing regions are the complements of those at volume 1 − V . At zero or full volume the conclusion is trivial.
